newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says no chance Germany to join jobs scheme.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says no chance Germany to join jobs scheme.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Sunday that there was no chance that Germany would agree to participate in a costly jobs-creation scheme with France.

"We will stick to our position that there will be no money flowing from Germany for additional jobs creation programmes," Waigel told Reuters on his way into a ceremony marking the 100th anniversary of the death of a German health spa pioneer.

Waigel, who later on Sunday heads for an EU summit meeting in Amsterdam, earlier told the Frankfurter Allgemeine Sonntagszeitung that Bonn has ruled out German participation in the Europe-wide job creation scheme France wants.
"I will not go along with (state job creation programmes) under which Germany pays one-third to Europe and gets only 15 percent back," Waigel told the Sunday newspaper.
The newspaper cited Waigel as saying he expected some form of agreement on employment strategy at the summit meeting but that this would not be tied in with additional spending.

He also said he was "cautiously optimistic" that the French government would ratify the stability pact designed to ensure fiscal displine under the future single currency, even after France expressed some reservations about the agreement.
The two-day Amsterdam summit, called to agree a new EU treaty, has been overshadowed by a rift between France and Germany over how to proceed toward monetary union.
The new socialist French government is insisting that the 18 million jobless in the EU be taken into account in any deal on Europe.
